clues.kinetics: Absolute bioavailability is approximately 80%, and about 50% is bound to plasma proteins. Renal elimination is the principal clearance route, and meals have no clinically relevant effect on exposure.
clues.substance: The active moiety has a molecular weight of 371.42, and the description names no salt form.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA as 1, 2 and 4 mg tablets, dosed once daily with minimal accumulation.
clues.safety: Boxed warning for serious infections, mortality, malignancy, major adverse cardiovascular events and thrombosis; no contraindications. Upper respiratory and urinary tract infections are the most common.
clues.indication: Moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis in adults with an inadequate response to one or more TNF blockers. Also COVID-19 in hospitalized adults, and severe alopecia areata.
clues.mechanism: It inhibits Janus kinase enzymes, blocking the phosphorylation and activation of STATs that transmit cytokine signals. Which JAK enzymes matter therapeutically is not known.

tell: A JAK inhibitor excreted mostly unchanged, 69% in urine, and a substrate of the OAT3 transporter.

evidence.pk.tmaxH: peak plasma concentrations are reached approximately at 1 hour
evidence.pk.halfLifeH: Elimination half-life in subjects with moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis and severe alopecia areata is approximately 12 to 16 hours
pill: The 4 mg tablet is medium pink, round
